basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 16.' and it opens 'Vers. 16. Egressusque Cain a facie Domini habitavit in terra profugus ad orientalem'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 16. Egressusque Cain a facie Domini habitavit in terra profugus ad orientalem plagam Eden. Eden epulae vel deliciae interpretatur. Septuaginta dicunt: habitavit in terra Naith. Sed Naith non est hoc loci nomen. Interpretatur autem instabilis vel vagus, et ideo in terra Naith habitare dicitur, quia instabilis et fluctuans vagabatur.
